representative_tasks.task: Build an implicit-feedback recommender from a purchase/click event log
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Sparse CSR user x item matrix with string ids and kept id mappings, ALS with confidence weighting (alpha) tuned on a held-out ranking metric, recommendations mapped back from internal indices to real item ids, already-seen items excluded

representative_tasks.task: Recommend similar items for a product page from titles and descriptions
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: TF-IDF over de-duplicated item metadata, cosine similarity with the seed item excluded explicitly, top-K neighbours

representative_tasks.task: Train a rating-prediction model on explicit 1-5 star ratings
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Surprise SVD with a Reader matching the rating scale, seeded KFold cross-validation of RMSE/MAE, with the caveat that ranking metrics judge the top-N list

representative_tasks.task: Serve recommendations to users who are new or have no history
representative_tasks.expected_outcome: Real-id entry point that routes unknown or zero-history users to a popularity/content fallback, and a hybrid blend of min-max-scaled CF and content scores for known users

negative_cases: A model evaluated only by Precision@10 on a random interaction split, beaten by a most-popular baseline (planned: time-based split, coverage, popularity bias)
Serving code that returns implicit's internal column indices as product ids (planned failure_recovery case)
rubric: Implicit counts treated as confidence (ALS/BPR), explicit ratings with SVD-style MF; not interchangeable
Ranking metrics (Precision@K, NDCG@K) and catalog coverage for top-N quality, on a time-based split when timestamps exist
Cold-start users and items get a popularity/content fallback, never a zero-vector or another user's index
Internal matrix indices are mapped back to real ids before serving
prerequisites: example-deps for executable tests: numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, implicit, scikit-surprise, threadpoolctl (see docs/EXAMPLE-TESTS.md)
execution_constraints: Offline grading and fixture self-tests need only Python 3.10+ stdlib and no network.
Executable tests need the example-test dependencies and run via run_evals.py --run-executable; the module ran in about 7 s on CPU (observed 2026-10-27).
Model-mode runs need --provider anthropic --model <id> --allow-network and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; they cost money and are not deterministic.
expected_artifacts: Sparse user x item CSR matrix plus user_ids / item_ids mappings
Fitted ALS model, Surprise SVD cross-validation report, Precision@10 / NDCG@10 / catalog coverage
recommend_for_user_id serving function with a popularity fallback
known_limitations: Hard assertions are regexes over the response text: they verify that key concepts are stated, not that the reasoning connecting them is correct.

Hard-assertion robustness is spot-checked only: an independent reviewer's held-out probe found most realistic on-topic wrong answers passed the first-draft must_not_include patterns. The patterns were broadened and those answers committed verbatim as .fail.adversarial*/.pass.blind fixtures; later probes were written by the pattern author and are not blind.
No baseline (with-skill vs without-skill) has been measured for this skill; any uplift claim requires a recorded or model run.
Executable tests use a small synthetic event log (tens of users and items); they prove index mapping, fallback routing and library behaviour, not recommendation quality on real data.
unsupported_use_cases: Generic supervised classification/regression on tabular data (supervised-learning)
Online A/B test design for recommenders (not covered by this skill)
